history.value: Claude Code, too slow for him
history.quote: When I use Claude’s Code, the terminal version of Claude … which is actually my preferred way of using it, I get too impatient.
I've thoroughly enjoyed putting them all to work in OpenCode, which is a terminal interface for coding agents

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: Reviewed with `codex review --base quattro` over eight passes; every finding was fixed, most with a regression test.

history.quote: This is all very evident if you've tried to employ any of the new models — especially Claude Opus 4.5, Codex 5, Gemini 3, and even the Chinese open-weight models like MiniMax M2.1 and GLM-4.7 — in one of the modern terminal harnesses that give them access to all these autonomous powers.
The Omarchy 4 branch is now 30,000 lines of new code. The majority of it was written by GPT5.5.
But GPT 5.6 Sol? 4m45s and it was done.

review_style.value: A second model reviews, then he reads the diff
review_style.quote: Reviewed with `codex review --base quattro` over eight passes; every finding was fixed, most with a regression test.

also.quote: Reviewed with Claude and addressed its LocalSend class mismatch, redundant catch-all rule findings, and the transparency shortcut behavior.
You still need to review, but there's just no way this scale of a conversion would be feasible without AI in a reasonable time.
NeoVim for reviewing diffs via Lazygit
